title: The decycling number of the 600-cell
statement: A decycling set (feedback vertex set) of a graph is a set of vertices whose removal leaves a forest. Determine the decycling number of the graph of the 600-cell {3,3,5} (120 vertices, 12-regular), equivalently the largest number of its vertices that induce a forest. Known: the largest induced forest has between 37 and 60 vertices (decycling number between 60 and 83); find an induced forest with 38 or more vertices.
submission: Text file: the vertex numbers (0 to 119) of the forest, separated by spaces or newlines, in the checker's vertex order (see cell600_graph in checkers/orig_comb.py).
score: the number of vertices of the induced forest (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: an induced forest on 37 vertices found by randomized greedy construction with exchange moves and by simulated annealing (tools/graph_sets.py, tools/forest_sa.py; both reach 37)

context: The decycling number was introduced by Beineke and Vandell (Decycling graphs, J. Graph Theory 25 (1997) 59-77) and is known exactly for few families; for hypercubes only bounds and small cases are known, and for random regular graphs it is studied asymptotically (e.g. arXiv:2003.00538 for 4-regular random graphs). In the 600-cell every edge lies in 5 triangles and every vertex in 20 tetrahedral cells, so an induced forest can take at most 2 vertices of each cell (three would form a triangle); counting cells gives at most 600 x 2 / 20 = 60 forest vertices, while our searches stop at 37. The gap is large, and a symmetric construction could close much of it.
references: L. W. Beineke, R. C. Vandell, Decycling graphs, J. Graph Theory 25 (1997) 59-77
On the decycling number of 4-regular random graphs, arXiv:2003.00538

novelty.verdict: new. No decycling, feedback-vertex-set or induced-forest result for the 600-cell (or other regular 4-polytopes) was found in our arXiv searches.
closest: Decycling numbers of hypercubes, grids and random regular graphs; the 600-cell graph is none of these.

baseline.text: 37 (decycling set of 83), held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the forest in `refs/cell600-forest.txt`. Upper bound 60: each of the 600 tetrahedral cells holds at most 2 forest vertices and each vertex lies in 20 cells.

bound.source: each tetrahedral cell holds at most 2 vertices of an induced forest; 20 cells per vertex
